{
  "anomaly_detected": true,
  "confidence": 0.45,
  "anomalies": [
    {
      "category": "polarity",
      "components": ["D4", "T5", "R32"],
      "pins": ["D4.2", "D4.1", "T5.1", "T5.2", "R32.1"],
      "nets": ["GND", "/+24V_{F}", "/NET0094"],
      "observed": "T5 (AON6407 P-channel) has its source on /+24V_{F} and drain on +24V, with its gate on /NET0094. That gate net contains only R32 (33k, pulled to /+24V_{F}), D4 (12V zener, cathode on the gate net, anode on GND) and T5 pin 1. Nothing drives the gate. With the zener anode at GND, the gate is clamped about 12 V above ground while the source sits at about 24 V, so Vgs is about -12 V and T5 is held on.",
      "expected": "A P-channel high-side switch should be off when its gate is pulled up to the source, and should have a gate clamp referenced to its source (zener between gate and source), with a drive path able to turn it on and off. The netlist shows no such drive path for T5.",
      "evidence": [
        {"source": "netlist", "quote": "(comp (ref \"D4\") (value \"12V\") ... (description \"Zener diode\")"},
        {"source": "netlist", "quote": "(net (code \"8\") ... (node (ref \"D4\") (pin \"2\") ...) ... (node (ref \"GND\") ...)"},
        {"source": "netlist", "quote": "(net (code \"63\") (name \"/NET0094\") (class \"Default\") (node (ref \"D4\") (pin \"1\") (pinfunction \"K\") ...) (node (ref \"R32\") (pin \"1\") ...) (node (ref \"T5\") (pin \"1\") (pinfunction \"G\") ...))"},
        {"source": "netlist", "quote": "(net (code \"6\") (name \"/+24V_{F}\") (class \"HighPower\") (node (ref \"D6\") ...) (node (ref \"F2\") (pin \"2\") ...) (node (ref \"R32\") (pin \"2\") ...) (node (ref \"T5\") (pin \"2\") (pinfunction \"S\") ...))"},
        {"source": "spec", "quote": "D1, D4 — SS34 Schottky | Flyback/reverse-current protection across inductive loads (pump/valve)"}
      ],
      "impact": "The T5 power switch cannot be turned off. The 24 V input path or the ATO valve stage it controls stays permanently conducting, so the intended switching or protection function does not work.",
      "confidence": 0.4
    },
    {
      "category": "open_connection",
      "components": ["U5"],
      "pins": ["U5.2"],
      "nets": [],
      "observed": "The TPS62933 buck regulator's EN pin (pin 2) is marked as unconnected (no_connect) and is not on any net. Its enable is therefore undefined, while VIN, RT, SS and FB are all wired.",
      "expected": "The EN pin of the TPS62933 should be tied to VIN, through a divider, or to a defined logic level, so that the 5 V rail has a defined enable state.",
      "evidence": [
        {"source": "netlist", "quote": "(net (code \"142\") (name \"unconnected-(U5-EN-Pad2)\") (class \"Default\") (node (ref \"U5\") (pin \"2\") (pinfunction \"EN\") (pintype \"input+no_connect\")))"}
      ],
      "impact": "If the EN pin has no internal pull, the +5 V rail may not start reliably, or may behave unpredictably. This would starve the ESP32 and the rest of the 5 V and 3.3 V domains.",
      "confidence": 0.3
    }
  ],
  "summary": "The buck-regulator enable is floating and the ATO/input P-channel switch T5 has a gate clamp returned to GND rather than its source, which leaves it permanently on with no drive input; the second item is less certain because the reference design may differ."
}

anomalies.observed: T5 (AON6407 P-channel) has its source on /+24V_{F} and drain on +24V, with its gate on /NET0094. That gate net contains only R32 (33k, pulled to /+24V_{F}), D4 (12V zener, cathode on the gate net, anode on GND) and T5 pin 1. Nothing drives the gate. With the zener anode at GND, the gate is clamped about 12 V above ground while the source sits at about 24 V, so Vgs is about -12 V and T5 is held on.

anomalies.impact: The T5 power switch cannot be turned off. The 24 V input path or the ATO valve stage it controls stays permanently conducting, so the intended switching or protection function does not work.

anomalies.expected: The EN pin of the TPS62933 should be tied to VIN, through a divider, or to a defined logic level, so that the 5 V rail has a defined enable state.
anomalies.impact: If the EN pin has no internal pull, the +5 V rail may not start reliably, or may behave unpredictably. This would starve the ESP32 and the rest of the 5 V and 3.3 V domains.
